q: Which sector has the largest share in India's GDP?
x: Services give more than half; farming under a fifth, but farming employs the most people.

q: Under which Five Year Plan was the Rolling Plan introduced?
x: The Rolling Plan (1978–80) was not one of the numbered Five Year Plans.

q: The Rolling Plan was adopted by the government of…
x: The Janata government, 1978. The idea came from Gunnar Myrdal.

q: In a Rolling Plan…
o: Both targets and money are revised every year
Targets are fixed for five years
Only money is revised every year
Plans are made only for one sector
x: It is checked every year and rolls one year forward.

q: The idea of a Rolling Plan is credited to…
x: Swedish economist Gunnar Myrdal.

q: Which statement about NITI Aayog is WRONG?
x: It has only a few full-time members.

q: Which committee suggested setting up the National Stock Exchange?
x: Pherwani (1991).

q: One tax in place of many indirect taxes is…
x: GST replaced excise, service tax, VAT and others.

q: The national Multidimensional Poverty Index uses data from the…
x: NITI Aayog uses NFHS data.

q: Which is NOT a real kind of deficit?
x: "Monetary deficit" was the wrong option in 2025.

q: Which is NOT a function of the RBI?
x: SEBI regulates stock exchanges.

q: Financial inclusion was first made a plan goal in the…
x: 11th Plan (2007–12): inclusive growth.

q: Who measures poverty in India now?
x: NITI Aayog.

q: Economic and social planning is in which list?
x: Entry 20 of the Concurrent List.

q: The best measure of economic growth of a country is…
x: Real income per person removes price rise and population growth.

q: Which body regulates insurance?
x: IRDAI, head office in Hyderabad.

q: Mutual funds are regulated by…
x: SEBI regulates stock exchanges, mutual funds and brokers.

q: What is the upper limit for an RTGS transfer?
x: Minimum ₹2 lakh; no maximum.

q: "Mercantile law" mainly means…
x: Business law, mainly the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

q: The UDYAMI helpline is for…
x: MSME helpline.

q: The First Five Year Plan was based on the…
x: First Plan (1951–56): farming and irrigation; Harrod–Domar model.

q: The Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur steel plants were set up under the…
x: The Second Plan (1956–61) stressed heavy industry.

q: Why did the Third Five Year Plan fail?
x: Wars with China (1962) and Pakistan (1965) and droughts. Then came a plan holiday (1966–69).

q: During the plan holiday (1966–69), India had…
x: Three one-year plans.

q: Banks were nationalised in 1969 during the…
x: Fourth Plan (1969–74).

q: "Garibi Hatao" is linked to which Plan?
x: Fifth Plan (1974–78), ended a year early.

q: The theme of the 12th Five Year Plan was…
o: Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth
x: 12th (2012–17). Inclusive growth was the 11th.

q: The Planning Commission was set up in…
x: March 1950, with the PM as chairman.

q: NITI Aayog was set up on…
x: By a cabinet decision; it is neither constitutional nor statutory.

q: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog includes…
x: All Chief Ministers (and Lt Governors of some UTs).

q: GDP is…
o: Value of all final goods and services produced inside a country in a year
Income of citizens anywhere in the world
x: GNP adds income Indians earn abroad and subtracts what foreigners earn here.

q: "Net" in national income means…
x: Net = gross minus depreciation (wear and tear).

q: "Real" GDP means GDP…
x: Real = at constant prices. Nominal = at current prices.

q: In 2025 India became the world's fourth largest economy by passing…
x: India passed Japan in 2025.

q: Revenue deficit minus grants for creating assets is called…
x: Effective revenue deficit.

q: Capital spending in the Union Budget 2026-27 is about…
x: Budget presented on 1 February 2026.

q: Which is a direct tax?
x: A direct tax is paid by the person it is charged on.

q: After the September 2025 GST change, the two main rates are…
x: Mainly 5% and 18%, with 40% on luxury and harmful goods.

q: Which is outside GST?
x: Alcohol for drinking is outside GST; petrol and diesel are outside for now.

q: The GST Council is headed by the…
x: Article 279A.

q: The RBI was set up on…
x: Set up in 1935, nationalised in 1949.

q: In which year was the RBI nationalised?
x: 1 January 1949.

q: Who is the present RBI Governor?
x: Sanjay Malhotra.

q: The rate at which the RBI lends to banks is the…
x: Raising the repo rate makes loans costlier and cools prices.

q: The share of deposits a bank must keep with the RBI in cash is…
x: Cash Reserve Ratio. SLR is kept in gold or government bonds.

q: SLR must be kept in the form of…
x: Statutory Liquidity Ratio: liquid assets held by the bank itself.

q: When the RBI buys or sells government bonds to change money supply, it is called…
x: Buying bonds adds money; selling removes it.

q: Which body handles farm and village credit?
x: NABARD. SIDBI handles small industries.

q: UPI is run by…
x: National Payments Corporation of India; UPI launched in 2016.

q: NEFT transfers are settled…
o: One by one in real time
x: NEFT works in batches and has no minimum; RTGS is one-by-one.

q: The Raja Chelliah Committee (1991) dealt with…
x: Chelliah = tax. Malhotra = insurance. Abid Hussain = small industries.

q: The Malhotra Committee (1993) was about…
x: It led to opening insurance to private firms.

q: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended…
x: It led to the 4% CPI target and the MPC.

q: The Tendulkar Committee (2009) worked on…
x: Tendulkar and Rangarajan both drew poverty lines.

q: Too much money chasing too few goods is called…
x: Cost-push comes from higher fuel, wages or raw material costs.

q: High prices and low growth together is called…
x: Stagflation.

q: When prices still rise but more slowly, it is called…
x: Deflation means prices actually fall.

q: The Wholesale Price Index is published by…
x: WPI: Commerce Ministry. CPI: National Statistics Office.

q: What is the new base year of the CPI?
x: CPI base 2024; GDP base 2022-23.

q: Skills not matching the jobs available causes…
x: Structural unemployment.

q: Jobs data in India comes from the…
x: PLFS.

q: About how many people came out of multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23?
x: NITI Aayog estimate: about 24.8 crore.

q: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) aims at…
o: A bank account for every family
x: Financial inclusion.

q: Mudra Yojana (2015) gives…
x: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency.

q: How much does PM-KISAN give a farmer each year?
x: In three instalments, since 2019.

q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY gives health cover of…
x: Launched in 2018.

q: SANKALP (2018) is a scheme for…
x: Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion.

q: Which month is observed as Nutrition Month (Poshan Maah)?
x: Under POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018).

q: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birthday of…
x: P.C. Mahalanobis.

q: FEMA (1999) replaced…
x: The stricter Foreign Exchange Regulation Act.

q: The Economic Survey is presented…
x: The Budget is on 1 February.

q: Which sector employs the largest number of people in India?
x: Small output, many workers: the main gap in India's economy.

q: Free food grain under PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana began in…
x: Started during COVID-19 in 2020.

q: MGNREGA, passed in 2005, promised how many days of paid work?
x: 100 days; the December 2025 VB–G RAM G Act raised it to 125.
